key_cases.case_name: Toensing v. Attorney Gen. of Vt.
key_cases.holding: Records produced or acquired in the course of agency business are public records under the Public Records Act even when they sit in employees' private accounts, and where a requester specifically seeks such communications the agency must ask the named employees to produce them.
key_cases.relevance: It establishes the documentary reach of any independent analysis of Vermont agency conduct.
key_cases.quote: the PRA's definition of "public record" includes digital documents stored in private accounts, but emphasize that it extends only to documents that otherwise meet the definition of public records

key_cases.case_name: In re Appeal of T.O. & L.O.
key_cases.holding: The Human Services Board lacked jurisdiction over grandparents' claim that DCF failed to comply with state and federal relative-placement requirements; their remedy lies in the family division of the superior court, and no due process violation resulted.
key_cases.relevance: The case exposes a structural accountability gap between federal relative-placement mandates and available Vermont remedies.
key_cases.quote: That procedure is access to the family division, not to the Human Services Board.

key_cases.holding: Termination was affirmed; a reasonable-efforts finding is a separate determination from the best-interests inquiry and is not a precondition to terminating parental rights, although the level of assistance given to parents remains relevant to whether they can resume parenting in a reasonable time.
key_cases.relevance: C.P. is the clearest statement of the structural gap between federal reasonable-efforts compliance and state termination outcomes in Vermont.
key_cases.quote: the court is not required to find DCF made reasonable efforts as a prerequisite to termination

key_cases.court: Supreme Court of the United States
key_cases.holding: The Due Process Clause requires a State to support its allegations by at least clear and convincing evidence before it may permanently terminate the rights of parents in their natural child, so New York's fair-preponderance standard was unconstitutional.
key_cases.relevance: Any systemic audit of Vermont's chain must test state practice against Santosky's constitutional floor for severing the parent-child relationship.
key_cases.quote: The fundamental liberty interest of natural parents in the care, custody, and management of their child does not evaporate simply because they have not been model parents
